result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.chromatic_number_upper_bound()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Get an upper bound on the chromatic number from a coloring. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L21781-L21826){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.chromatic_number_upper_bound(coloring=None) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} The chromatic number is the minimum number of colors needed to color a graph. This method returns the number of distinct colors used in a coloring, which provides an upper bound. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [coloring]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [dict[int, int] | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : A dictionary mapping node IDs to colors. If `None`, computes a greedy coloring first using the `"largest_first"` strategy. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The number of distinct colors used in the coloring. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} A triangle requires 3 mutually distinct colors, so its chromatic number (and the upper bound this method returns) is exactly 3: ::: {#70892783 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph(directed=False) .add_node(label="A") .add_node(label="B") .add_node(label="C") .add_edge("A", "B") .add_edge("B", "C") .add_edge("C", "A") ) # Get upper bound using a default greedy coloring graph.chromatic_number_upper_bound() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` 3 ``` ::: :::
